column2: Used if no valid personality found
column5: Se utiliza cuando no se encuentra una personalidad válida para el cargo.

column2: Local tyrant rules his nation with iron-fisted terror. Due to his nation's limited power he rarely supports expansionist acts - in fact, he often owes his power to foreign dictator - but as for centralizing all the power in his country to his own hands, there are no ways to avoid.
column5: Gobierna con puño de hierro. Debido al poder limitado de su país rara vez emprende expansión exterior, pero centraliza implacablemente todo el poder nacional en sus manos.

column2: The Biased Intellectual is a refined academic intellectual, whose scholarly work has biased his judgment of other countries and people. The Biased Intellectual is often arrogant and witty about those he dislikes but fawning and ingratiating towards those he likes.
column5: Académico refinado cuyos prejuicios nublan su criterio diplomático. Suele ser arrogante y mordaz con quienes rechaza, pero extremadamente complaciente con sus aliados predilectos.

column2: The Ideological Crusader views himself as a devoted proponent of his political system, but to others he is an extremist. If a Fascist, he judges all non-Fascists as weak and decadent. If a Democrat, he would rather lose a war than comply with any demands from a non-Democrat. If a Communist, he views Democrats as evil capitalists and Fascists as evil pseudo-capitalists. When it comes to ideology it is impossible to argue with him since he has already found his salvation.
column5: Defensor fanático de su sistema político que no admite concesiones. Prefiere la derrota antes que pactar con ideologías contrarias, considerándolas decadentes o enemigas.

column2: The Apologetic Clerk is often a brilliant man, but either lacks inner strength or is so filled with doubt over the political system of his own country that he can seldom stay consistent. An Apologetic Clerk might also be a man who truly believes in the righteousness of his political system, but unfortunately also believes that the other side will win the war.
column5: Hombre brillante pero inseguro y dubitativo. Su constante falta de confianza en la victoria de su nación o en su propio sistema político lo hace errático y vacilante.

column2: The Iron-Fisted Brute is a simple man who has risen through the ranks of the military or the party. He views the world in black and white: those who eat and those who are eaten. Often brutish and sometimes a sociopath, the Iron-Fisted Brute makes policies without remorse.
column5: Surgido del ejército o del partido, ve el mundo como una lucha sin cuartel. Despiadado y autoritario, aplica medidas coercitivas extremas sin remordimiento alguno.

column2: The Great Compromiser is an easy-going and amiable fellow liked by most. Often he is a sage-like old man and a professional diplomat with many years of service, tactful and experienced. He has the ability to forge lasting friendships and to bind the wills of many into one, striving towards the same goal.
column5: Diplomático veterano, prudente y respetado. Sobresale forjando alianzas duraderas, mediando en disputas y uniendo voluntades opuestas hacia un objetivo común.

column2: The General Staffer is a former military man, perhaps a former teacher of strategy in the General Staff. He has now resettled in the field of Foreign Affairs, a subject that was always his 'hobby'. The General Staffer most likely follows his old military notion of politics and is focused on diplomacy through military might. However, by doing that, the General Staffer is often deemed a simple-minded man, lacking in imagination and boring.
column5: Exmilitar metido a diplomático que gestiona la política exterior como una campaña militar. Prioriza la fuerza bruta pero carece de flexibilidad, tacto e inventiva.

column2: The Cloak-and-Dagger Schemer is a secretive person. He prefers unorthodox plans and constantly seeks weaknesses to exploit among his slower victims. Often the Cloak-and-Dagger Schemer has a background in the Secret Service and that experience makes him sly and uninformative. Basically the Cloak-and-Dagger Schemer is not a great diplomat but he is so unpredictable that in the end he often gets what he wants.
column5: Procedente del espionaje, es reservado y retorcido. Diseña maniobras impredecibles y aprovecha los puntos débiles de rivales lentos para imponer sus fines.

column2: The Administrative Genius is an ardent laborer, who uses his personnel and modern techniques to the utmost to improve the war effort. The Administrative Genius is often a young engineer or scientist, free-thinking and innovative. He always tries to be 'objective' and 'impartial' to further the common good.
column5: Técnico meticuloso e innovador. Optimiza al máximo la burocracia, la gestión de personal y los recursos modernos para sostener con eficacia el esfuerzo nacional.

column2: The Resource Industrialist is usually a civilian from the heavy industry sector who has been appointed to govern the nation's industrial efforts. He always tries to run the country as he would the coal mine back home, improving and expanding its base. As such he is a great organizer, but he sometimes tends to neglect the finer points of the armaments industry.
column5: Magnate de la industria pesada que gestiona la economía como una gran explotación minera. Excelente ampliando la base extractiva, aunque descuida el armamento sofisticado.

column2: The Laissez-Faire Capitalist is a specialist in market economics. It is his firmest opinion that little government intervention is needed, but that the good old invisible hand will best direct the resources of the Nation, war or no war.
column5: Partidario del libre mercado a ultranza. Cree firmemente que el Estado no debe intervenir y que las leyes del mercado deben regular la distribución de recursos.

column2: The Theoretical Scientist is a brilliant old professor picked out from the nation's leading university. He is of course a specialist in science both theoretical and applied. However he sometimes has a hard time prioritizing military matters, when great exploits in the civilian sectors can be attained. This often makes him a proponent of the more neutral areas of Electronics and Communication, but sometimes if he is eccentric enough, Secret Weapons are his preferred field.
column5: Académico brillante que prioriza la investigación científica. Aunque a veces relega las urgencias castrenses, potencia campos tecnológicos avanzados y armas secretas.

column2: The Military Entrepreneur is a former military man, possibly an old fighter from the Great War. He knows his priority and that is to get the guns and the butter to the troops at the front. This priority often leads to the neglect of the finer points of science
column5: Veterano práctico enfocado en asegurar que no falten suministros, armas y raciones a las tropas del frente, sacrificando la investigación científica avanzada.

column2: The Battle Fleet Proponent is not only an able administrator and politician, he is also a meddler in Grand Strategy. He believes that battleships are what the country needs.
column5: Promotor incondicional de los acorazados y los grandes navíos artilleros. Está convencido de que solo una flota masiva de combate asegura la victoria en el mar.

column2: The Submarine Proponent is not only an able administrator and politician, but he also is meddling in the area of Grand Strategy. He believes that submarines are now the decisive weapon of naval warfare.
column5: Estratega naval convencido de que los sumergibles representan el arma definitiva para estrangular el tráfico mercantil y aniquilar al enemigo con poco coste.

column2: The Tank Proponent is not only an able administrator and politician, but he also is meddling in the area of Grand Strategy. He believes that tanks are now the most vital weapon of war.
column5: Defiende que los carros blindados y las unidades móviles son la clave de la guerra moderna, priorizando la fabricación e investigación de divisiones acorazadas.

column2: The Infantry Proponent is not only an able administrator and politician, but he also is meddling in the area of Grand Strategy. He believes that Infantry is still the most important fighting force.
column5: Tradicionalista castrense que sostiene que la infantería sigue siendo el pilar fundamental en campaña, priorizando el reclutamiento masivo y el armamento a pie.

column2: The Air-to-Ground Proponent is not only an able administrator and politician, but he also is meddling in the area of Grand Strategy. He believes that bombing is the best way to defeat the enemy army.
column5: Defiende que la aviación táctica y de ataque al suelo es la herramienta primordial para quebrar y aniquilar a los ejércitos enemigos en coordinación con tierra.

column2: The Air-to-Sea Proponent is not only an able administrator and politician, but he also is meddling in the area of Grand Strategy. He believes that bombing is now the best way to defeat the enemy's navy.
column5: Sostiene que la aviación naval y el torpedeo aéreo han vuelto obsoletas a las grandes flotas, destinando recursos al ataque aéreo antibuque.

column2: The Strategic Air Proponent is not only an able administrator and politician, but he also is meddling in the area of Grand Strategy. He believes that bombing the enemy's industry is now the way to win the war.
column5: Partidario de ganar la guerra mediante bombardeos masivos de largo alcance que destruyan los centros industriales y la moral de la población adversaria.

column2: The Silent Lawyer directs his department with little imagination and creativity, but he is just.
column5: Administrador metódico, inflexible e imparcial. Dirige su área sin grandes alardes de inventiva, apegándose siempre a la más estricta legalidad y justicia.

column2: The Compassionate Gentleman is a jovial man who wishes to please all. The population like him, but he is known to be soft on crimes and terrorism.
column5: Figura amable y estimada por la ciudadanía que intenta contentar a todos. Sin embargo, su excesiva indulgencia debilita la seguridad y el castigo del delito.

column2: The Crime Fighter has devoted his life to combating crime. The people like his firm grip and feel reassured that they are safe.
column5: Dedicado en cuerpo y alma a erradicar la delincuencia mediante mano dura y control riguroso, transmitiendo gran sensación de seguridad a la población.

column2: The Prince of Terror lives by the rule: it is better to be feared than to be loved. However, extreme violence may actually increase dissent, a factor the Prince of Terror is unable to see.
column5: Aplica la máxima de que es mejor ser temido que amado. Su uso indiscriminado del terror y la represión sofoca revueltas, pero suele avivar el rencor popular.

column2: The Back Stabber uses his position to root out dissent and disloyal elements within the elite, but he is unable to cope with occupied territories because of his lack of trustworthiness.
column5: Especialista en purgar facciones disidentes entre la élite gubernamental, aunque su naturaleza desleal lo incapacita para apaciguar regiones conquistadas.

column2: The Man of the People knows how to talk to both high and low in society. For him it is a crusade to ease the burden of the poor. However, he is in an awkward position when trying to help people in the occupied zones, and his hands are bound by the military.
column5: Líder carismático y cercano que busca mejorar la vida ciudadana y movilizar al pueblo, aunque ve restringida su influencia en las zonas de ocupación militar.

column2: The Efficient Sociopath has no remorse and uses any means necessary to further his goals. However, he always works in the shadows, trying to hide his personal perversions and the excess violence of his minions from the population and his fellow ministers.
column5: Frío y maquiavélico, emplea cualquier método sin escrúpulos ni remordimientos. Actúa en la sombra para encubrir sus abusos y la brutalidad de sus subordinados.

column2: The Technical Specialist concentrates his effort on the study of the modernization of foreign equipment and units to draw conclusions on how to best defeat them.
column5: Analista de inteligencia que examina al detalle el material y avances tecnológicos del enemigo para diseñar contramedidas y explotar sus vulnerabilidades.

column2: The Logistics Specialist uses the old General Staff technique of monitoring the movement of supplies to learn where a new threat is mounting.
column5: Supervisa minuciosamente el movimiento de convoyes y suministros rivales para prever con notable antelación dónde planea el enemigo concentrar sus ofensivas.

column2: The Political Specialist uses his 'technical embassy personnel' to fight a secret war of counter-intelligence with the enemy.
column5: Utiliza las redes diplomáticas y el personal consular como tapadera para librar una silenciosa guerra de espionaje y contrainteligencia contra el adversario.

column2: The Dismal Enigma is a man of secrets, and if he were not able to produce an 'Ace of Intelligence' from time to time he would have had lost his job ages ago.
column5: Hombre reservado y misterioso. Pese a su opacidad, conserva el puesto gracias a golpes maestros de espionaje que aportan informes determinantes de tanto en tanto.

column2: The Industrial Specialist concentrates his efforts on studying open industrial and economic sources of the enemy and thus often learns what will come by analyzing what they are producing at the moment.
column5: Deduce las intenciones militares enemigas analizando fuentes económicas abiertas, cifras fabriles y estadísticas de producción de materias primas.

column2: The Naval Intelligence Specialist uses the old Naval Staff technique of monitoring the basing of ships to learn where a new threat is mounting.
column5: Rastrea los movimientos de flotas y apostaderos marítimos del enemigo para identificar las zonas donde se gesta una amenaza anfibia o de bloqueo naval.

column2: This Chief of Staff teaches that Maneuver and Speed are the essence of modern warfare.
column5: Doctrina que consagra la rapidez de movimientos y la maniobra envolvente como los pilares determinantes del combate moderno sobre el terreno.

column2: This Chief of Staff teaches that Fire Support is the essence of modern warfare.
column5: Doctrina que prioriza la concentración masiva de artillería y apoyo de fuego como elemento decisivo para demoler las líneas defensivas enemigas.

column2: This Chief of Staff believes in the People's War and teaches that mass formations and guerrilla tactics are the essence of modern warfare.
column5: Doctrina basada en la guerra popular que enfatiza el despliegue de grandes masas combatientes y tácticas de desgaste para abrumar al invasor.

column2: This Chief of Staff teaches that morale and small-unit leadership are the essence of modern warfare.
column5: Doctrina orientada a potenciar la moral combativa, la iniciativa táctica en unidades pequeñas y el liderazgo de los cuadros de mando en el frente.

column2: This Chief of Staff teaches that Fortifications, Militia and Strategic Depth are the essence of modern warfare.
column5: Doctrina centrada en defensas fortificadas, milicias y profundidad estratégica para frenar y agotar cualquier avance de las columnas enemigas.

column2: This Chief of the Army directs the utilization of the ground forces by the doctrine of Elastic Defense. This means that deploying a thin defensive line with heavily armed infantry and deploying replacements and assault teams in the second lines are essential for wearing down the enemy and for winning the war.
column5: Doctrina que despliega una línea inicial de contención apoyada por fuertes reservas y fuerzas de asalto escalonadas listas para contraatacar.

column2: This Chief of the Army directs the utilization of the ground forces according to the doctrine of Static Defense. This means that deploying several defensive lines with fortified infantry and substantial artillery assets in the rear are essential for wearing down the enemy and for winning the war.
column5: Doctrina que plantea líneas atrincheradas profundas con potente artillería de apoyo para resistir cualquier asalto frontal de desgaste.

column2: This Chief of the Army directs the utilization of the ground forces according to the doctrine of Decisive Battle. This means that concentrating large amounts of superior attacking troops and forcing the enemy to commit inferior troops are essential for wearing down the enemy and for winning the war.
column5: Doctrina orientada a concentrar una masa ofensiva aplastante para forzar un enfrentamiento definitivo y aniquilar al grueso de las fuerzas enemigas.

column2: This Chief of the Army directs the utilization of the ground forces according to the doctrine of Armored Spearheads. This means that spearheading speedy offensives with tank units followed up with encircling infantry are essential for wearing down the enemy and for winning the war.
column5: Doctrina que emplea puntas de lanza acorazadas rápidas seguidas por infantería para perforar el frente y cercar a las divisiones enemigas.

column2: This Chief of the Army directs the utilization of the ground forces according to the doctrine of Guns and Butter. This means allowing the operational commanders freedom of command while ensuring the best possible supplies and training for the Army are essential for wearing down the enemy and for winning the war.
column5: Doctrina que combina una logística impecable e instrucción avanzada con amplia libertad operativa para los comandantes en el campo de batalla.

column2: This Chief of the Navy directs the utilization of the Naval forces according to the doctrine of Open Seas. This means that the control of sea lanes to far-flung resources is essential for winning the war.
column5: Doctrina naval enfocada en asegurar las líneas de comunicación marítimas y garantizar el flujo de recursos estratégicos desde ultramar.

column2: This Chief of the Navy directs the utilization of the Naval forces according to the doctrine of Decisive Battle. This means that in order to win the war it is essential to amass a large battle fleet and destroy the enemy's force on the High Seas.
column5: Doctrina naval que busca concentrar el grueso de la flota de combate para destruir la armada enemiga en una única gran batalla en alta mar.

column2: This Chief of the Navy directs the utilization of the Naval forces according to the doctrine of Power Projection, which means that by concentrating all power from aircraft, torpedoes and artillery fire into a suitable area a good chance for winning the war is ensured.
column5: Doctrina naval que concentra de manera coordinada aviación, torpedos y artillería pesada en sectores clave para imponer superioridad absoluta.

column2: This Chief of the Navy directs the utilization of the Naval forces according to the doctrine of Indirect Approach. This means that in order to win the war it is essential to avoid decisive battle and instead destroy the enemy's convoys and warships piecemeal.
column5: Doctrina que evita choques frontales con la flota enemiga y se enfoca en hundir sus convoyes y desgastar sus buques de forma gradual.

column2: This Chief of the Navy directs the utilization of the Naval forces according to the doctrine of Base Control. This means that in order to win the war it is essential to strike directly at the enemy bases (ports and islands), and take control of them with air and land forces.
column5: Doctrina naval que persigue la captura y destrucción de bases insulares y puertos enemigos combinando asaltos anfibios y apoyo aéreo.

column2: This Chief of the Air Force directs the utilization of the air force according to the doctrine of Air Superiority. This means that in order to win the war it is essential to control the skies above the battlefield.
column5: Doctrina aérea que considera el control indisputable del espacio aéreo sobre el frente como requisito imprescindible para cualquier victoria militar.

column2: This Chief of the Air Force directs the utilization of the air force according to the doctrine of Naval Aviation. This means that in order to win the war it is essential to work closely with the Navy and destroy the enemy Navy, preferably by bombing it to pieces.
column5: Doctrina orientada a coordinar estrechamente la aviación con la flota de guerra para localizar y demoler las agrupaciones navales del enemigo.

column2: This Chief of the Air Force directs the utilization of the Air forces according to the doctrine of Army Aviation. This means that in order to win the war it is essential to work closely with the Army and destroy the enemy land forces, preferably by bombing them to pieces.
column5: Doctrina orientada a emplear el poder aéreo en apoyo directo y constante de las tropas terrestres para pulverizar la resistencia en el frente.

column2: This Chief of the Air Force directs the utilization of the Air forces according to the doctrine of Carpet Bombing. This means that in order to win the war it is essential to grind down the enemy transportation network and industrial plants, and to demoralize his population by terror bombing.
column5: Doctrina que preconiza el bombardeo masivo de ciudades, fábricas y redes de transporte para quebrar la capacidad industrial y la moral del rival.

column2: This Chief of the Air Force directs the utilization of the Air forces according to the doctrine of Vertical Envelopment. This means that in order to win the war it is essential to seize strategic terrain or bridgeheads by air to quickly enable the Army to achieve a breakthrough.
column5: Doctrina que emplea fuerzas paracaidistas para tomar cabezas de puente y posiciones clave en la retaguardia enemiga y facilitar el avance terrestre.

column2: The Undistinguished Suit is an invisible minister. No one has ever heard of him and no one can remember his looks. He is famous for absolutely nothing.
column5: Burócrata inadvertido y gris que carece de méritos memorables. No suscita adhesiones ni rechazos, cumpliendo sus tareas sin pena ni gloria.

column2: The Air Superiority Proponent is not only an able administrator and politician, but he also is meddling in the area of Grand Strategy. He believes that control of the air is now most important aspect of war.
column5: Promotor incondicional de los cazas que insiste en que dominar el cielo sobre cualquier otro aspecto militar es el factor decisivo para vencer.

column2: The Corrupt Kleptocrat is a competent administrator, but he is thoroughly corrupt so military aid and military supplies regularly end up in the pockets of the minister and his cronies.
column5: Administrador capaz pero corrupto hasta la médula -  desvía con frecuencia suministros y partidas del presupuesto hacia su círculo cercano.

column2: The Crooked Kleptocrat ignores the crimes of the high and low and cares little about insurrections but other ministers are loyal towards him because of their chances for self-enrichment.
column5: Tolera la corrupción generalizada e ignora la criminalidad interna, asegurándose la complicidad de otros cargos deseosos de enriquecerse.

column2: The Power-Hungry Demagogue is an angry vengeful man full of hatred. However he possesses a demonic charisma that enchants the frustrated masses. He has but one real purpose and that is to control and shape the world into one of his liking.
column5: Orador encendido y rencoroso con un carisma magnético sobre las masas. Su único propósito es acaparar poder ilimitado y moldear el país a su antojo.

column2: The Barking Buffoon is a great political dramatic actor. People see him as a strong and competent leader who will save the nation and restore it to its historical greatness. But behind his mask of bombastic rhetoric hides a weak-minded, vain simpleton. Those who really know him, know he is an incompetent man.
column5: Actor histriónico tras cuya retórica grandilocuente de grandeza nacional se oculta una profunda incompetencia y un carácter vanidoso y errático.

column2: The Stern Imperialist is a staunch nationalist. He is neither charming nor an administrative genius. However he has one big asset, namely his fanatical determination to improve his nation's status. He will use any means to achieve that goal, be it political or military.
column5: Nacionalista inflexible que carece de tacto, pero posee una determinación de hierro para engrandecer a su país mediante la presión armada o diplomática.

column2: The Ruthless Powermonger treats his country and his people as personal possessions. He is completely unscrupulous and he will let nothing stand between him and his goals. Sometimes he can develop a streak of paranoia which will endanger friend and foe alike.
column5: Considera el Estado como su patrimonio personal. Cruel, paranoico y desprovisto de escrúpulos, elimina sin titubeos a cualquier obstáculo o rival.

column2: The Autocratic Charmer uses his charisma and ruthlessness to stay in power. He charms friend and foe alike and is an excellent negotiator. However, day-to-day governing is not his style and corruption flourishes under his rule.
column5: Seductor y negociador brillante que combina carisma con crueldad para perpetuarse. Descuida la gestión cotidiana, permitiendo que prospere la corrupción.

column2: The Resigned Generalissimo came to power to save his country from the ruin of anarchy and popular sentiment. He is tired of political bickering and tries to run the country as he used to command his regiment. Still, he is a competent and decisive man.
column5: Militar pragmático que asumió el poder para evitar el colapso del orden. Gobierna con disciplina marcial y decisión, hastiado de las intrigas políticas.

column2: The Benevolent Gentleman is charismatic and a master at winning elections. However, he lacks the character to be truly successful at the nation's helm. When things get rough, he merely smiles and waits out the winds of political opinion.
column5: Político carismático y hábil candidato electoral, aunque débil de carácter. Ante crisis graves, tiende a contemporizar a la espera de que amaine el temporal.

column2: The Weary Stiff-Neck is not the right man for this job. He tries to compensate for this with an aristocratic manner and stiff-necked acting. When it comes to politics he is weary and indecisive, always fearing that his lack of talent will show through his facade.
column5: Aristócrata estirado e incompetente. Oculta su inseguridad y cansancio tras una fachada distante, mostrándose vacilante en momentos cruciales.

column2: The Insignificant Layman lacks any kind of ambition or political interest. The only reason people do not move against him is that he is fairly harmless and there is no better replacement.
column5: Figura dócil y anodina sin vocación de mando ni peso político. Se mantiene en su cargo simplemente por ser inofensivo y por falta de un relevo claro.

column2: The Die-Hard Reformer wants to promote his political values and preferred system of government to other countries. He is willing to intervene politically and military to achieve his goals.
column5: Cruzado doctrinario empeñado en expandir su sistema de gobierno al extranjero mediante intervención armada o presiones diplomáticas activas.

column2: The Pig-Headed Isolationist is determined to keep his country out of war, and the mess of international politics. He might like or dislike international cooperation, but it is always national autonomy that is his goal.
column5: Aislacionista obstinado resuelto a mantener al país fuera de pugnas internacionales y alianzas militares, priorizando siempre la autonomía interna.

column2: The Popular Figurehead has little power due to the system of government in his country. But due to his popularity, any firm statement of his will have to be taken into consideration by those who have power in the country.
column5: Símbolo con escaso poder efectivo pero inmenso arrastre popular. Sus opiniones públicas obligan al gobierno real a replantearse sus medidas.

column2: The Silent Workhorse compensates for his lack of charisma with hard work and competence. He rarely takes pride of place, instead letting the Head of State shine in the sun while he gets the job done.
column5: Compensa su discreción pública con una capacidad de trabajo asombrosa, sosteniendo con eficiencia la maquinaria del Estado entre bambalinas.

column2: The Naive Optimist is a competent administrator and politician. However, he often succumbs to wishful thinking and fails to grasp the traps which have been laid for him.
column5: Político bienintencionado pero confiado en exceso. Tiende a subestimar peligros evidentes y cae fácilmente en celadas diplomáticas y políticas.

column2: The Flamboyant Tough Guy is a natural leader and a real fighter. He will try to avoid conflict but, if forced to, he will fight to the bitter end. His showmanship generates many creative ideas which he will defend with the stubbornness of a mule, whether they are good or bad.
column5: Líder temperamental y batallador. Procura esquivar choques innecesarios, pero empujado a la lid combate con tenacidad feroz e ideas extravagantes.

column2: The Happy Amateur got his position by pure chance and knows nothing of politics or government. However overwhelmed by the surprise of being in office, his ever-smiling face gives him an aura of confidence. Luckily for him, the people are unaware of his staggering incompetence.
column5: Llegó al cargo por azar y desconoce la gestión de gobierno, aunque su entusiasmo y semblante tranquilo enmascaran una pasmosa incompetencia.

column2: The Backroom Backstabber is a political veteran with years of experience as a party whip and senior party member. No intrigue will oust him and no foreign government can topple him. Foreign governments have to be very cautious around him though.
column5: Veterano de las intrigas partidarias y los pasillos de poder. Imposible de derrocar internamente, exige extrema cautela en la mesa de negociación.

column2: The Smiling Oilman is a self-made man and a former CEO of a large Oil Company. His experience, and some say his money, have brought him into office. However, he lacks political skill and is a novice in the international arena. At least he is thick-skinned, competent and a fast learner.
column5: Magnate pragmático que aprendió a desenvolverse en los negocios. Aunque novato en diplomacia, es duro en el trato, resuelto y aprende con notable rapidez.

column2: The Old General was appointed because of his power base and sometimes because of his glorious past. Not very interested or skilled in politics, he pursues his foremost interest: the state of the Army.
column5: General tradicionalista que debe su rango al prestigio militar pretérito. Ajeno a disquisiciones civiles, su única meta es preservar el ejército de tierra.

column2: The Old Admiral was appointed because of his power base and sometimes because of his glorious past. Not very interested or skilled in politics, he pursues his foremost interest: the state of the Navy.
column5: Marino de la vieja escuela encumbrado por glorias pasadas. Desinteresado de la política de partidos, defiende a capa y espada los intereses navales.

column2: The Air Marshal was appointed because of his power base and sometimes because of his glorious past. Not very interested or skilled in politics, he pursues his foremost interest: the state of the Air Force.
column5: Veterano de la aviación aupado por su veteranía bélica. Canaliza toda su influencia política para ampliar los medios y presupuestos de la fuerza aérea.

column2: The Political Protégé is a political crony, a confidant of the Head of State. He is neither very liked nor very competent. He was chosen because he was loyal and had a large net of contacts.
column5: Incondicional del jefe del Estado seleccionado por lealtad ciega y contactos más que por mérito o aptitudes reales de administración.

column2: The Ambitious Union Boss is a harsh man who turned to politics to get the power to change things. He is still a man of the working class but his new environment has curbed his radicalism. He is a tough negotiator but lacks administrative skill. His background is also a liability in some circumstances.
column5: Sindicalista curtido de extracción obrera metido a gobernar. Negociador tenaz e inflexible, aunque flojo en labores burocráticas y de gabinete.

column2: The Corporate Suit has spent his life in the business world, far away from politics. He was originally brought in as an independent minister, but due his competence and cooperation skills he has reached the top. He has formed a large network of contacts, but he is out of place in politics.
column5: Tecnócrata procedente del ámbito corporativo. Destaca por su rigor gerencial y contactos mercantiles, si bien desentona ante los ardides de la política.

column2: The Oil Baron is a powerful person in the oil industry. He controls or has connections with many industries and companies and he has a positive influence in the oil extraction and refining business.
column5: Magnate influyente del sector petrolero. Sus vínculos comerciales y conocimiento del negocio potencian notablemente la extracción y el refinado de crudo.

column2: The Steel Magnate has a prominent place in the steel making industry and is a key person in the steel markets. He can use his position to increase the productivity of his industries and boost the production and sale of metal products in his country.
column5: Figura destacada de la industria siderúrgica que aprovecha sus plantas y contactos para maximizar la producción, fundición y abastecimiento de metales.

column2: The Industrial Chemist has a important position the chemical industry. He uses his knowledge to develop new substances, processes and products and to increase scientific knowledge.
column5: Científico vinculado a la industria química que emplea su pericia para diseñar nuevos procesos y acelerar la investigación aplicada de materiales.

column2: The Media Magnate is a person with a dominant position in a media enterprise. He usually owns one or more newspapers or radio networks and can use them to influence the public opinion.
column5: Propietario de importantes diarios y emisoras de radio que aprovecha su control mediático para encauzar con eficacia la opinión pública nacional.

column2: Ferdinand Foch was a French soldier and military theorist. His thinking on military doctrine was shaped by the unshakeable belief, uncommon at the time, that the will to conquer is the first condition of victory. He was able to defend against overwhelming forces and his subsequent counterattacks were often successful.
column5: Ferdinand Foch fue un mariscal y teórico francés que sostenía que la voluntad de vencer es la base del triunfo -  destacó resistiendo y contraatacando con éxito.

column2: Paul von Hindenburg was a Prussian/German field marshal. Though Hindenburg was only average in terms of military ability, he had a team of talented and able subordinates who won him a series of great victories. These victories transformed Hindenburg into Germany's most popular man. During the war, there were wooden statues of Hindenburg built all over Germany, onto which people nailed money and cheques for war bonds.
column5: Paul von Hindenburg, mariscal alemán de dotes normales respaldado por un brillante equipo de oficiales. Sus victorias lo convirtieron en un icono popular.

column2: Luigi Cadorna was an Italian Field Marshal, most famous for being the chief of staff of the Italian army during the first part of World War I. Historians describe Cadorna as a martinet, ruthless with his troops and dismissive of his country's political authorities. During the course of war he fired 217 officers and executed at least 750 soldiers. Until the end he stubbornly refused to admit responsibility for his defeats.
column5: Luigi Cadorna fue un mariscal italiano célebre por su dureza inflexible, destituciones constantes y castigos draconianos, reacio a asumir sus reveses en el frente.

column2: Aleksei Alekseevich Brusilov was a Russian general most noted for the development of new offensive tactics used by the Imperial Russian Army. Brusilov used smaller specialized units of soldiers to attack weak points in the enemy trench lines and blow open holes for the rest of the Army to advance into.
column5: Aleksei Brusílov fue un general ruso innovador que desarrolló ofensivas coordinadas con pequeñas unidades de choque para abrir brechas en las trincheras.

column2: Wilhelm II, born Frederick William Victor Albert of Prussia, was crowned German Emperor and King of Prussia on 15 June 1888. During his reign, he supported various laws which improved working conditions, protected women and children and regulated labor relations. In Foreign policy, he undertook various spectacular acts in the international sphere that led to frictions with many European countries. In the military sphere, he decided to pursue a policy of massive naval construction, but he let his generals influence him and dictate his policy.
column5: Guillermo II, emperador de Alemania, impulsó el rearme naval y acciones exteriores sonadas que provocaron tensiones, muy influenciado por sus generales.

column2: Nicholas II was crowned Emperor and Autocrat of All the Russias on 26 May 1896. Under his rule, Russia was defeated in the Russo-Japanese War, anti-semitic pogroms were encouraged and rebellions against the government crippled the country.
column5: Nicolás II, último autócrata de Rusia -  durante su mandato el imperio padeció la derrota ante Japón, graves disturbios sociales y una profunda crisis interna.

column2: Georges Benjamin Clemenceau was a French statesman, physician, journalist who became Prime Minister of France. He is commonly nicknamed Le Tigre (The Tiger) for his determination as a wartime leader.
column5: Georges Clemenceau, conocido como "El Tigre", primer ministro francés célebre por su indomable tesón y energía para dirigir el esfuerzo bélico hasta el final.

column2: Franz Joseph I was Emperor of Austria, King of Bohemia, King of Croatia and Apostolic King of Hungary since 2 December 1848. Durign his reign, he faced several failures of Austrian external and internal policy like the rise of power of Prussia, the unification of Italy and the Austro-Hungarian Compromise of 1867. Despite the military failures, Franz Joseph remained immensely respected and his patriarchal authority held the Empire together.
column5: Francisco José I rigió el Imperio austrohúngaro durante décadas -  pese a los reveses militares y crisis políticas, su figura patriarcal mantuvo unido al Estado.

column2: Thomas Woodrow Wilson was the 28th President of the United States. In foreign policy, he campaigned for neutrality and avoidance of open conflicts. He focused on diplomacy and financial considerations, leaving the waging of the war primarily in the hands of the Army. He promoted the idea of self-determination and thus revolutionized international diplomacy.
column5: Woodrow Wilson, 28.º presidente de EE. UU., promovió el principio de autodeterminación, la diplomacia internacional y la creación de una liga de naciones en paz.

column2: Adolf Hitler was an Austrian-born German politician and the leader of the National Socialist German Workers Party, commonly known as the Nazi Party. He Became absolute dictator of Germany in 1934, with the title of chancellor from 1933 and with the title head of state (Führer und Reichskanzler) from 1934 onwards.
column5: Dictador absoluto de Alemania y líder del partido nazi desde 1933-1934, instauró un régimen totalitario expansionista que desembocó en la guerra total.

column2: Joseph Vissarionovich Stalin was the first General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union's Central Committee in 1922. In the years following Lenin's death in 1924, he rose to become the leader of the Soviet Union.
column5: Secretario general del Partido Comunista y máximo mandatario de la Unión Soviética tras 1924, dirigió una industrialización forzosa y purgas implacables.

column2: Sir Winston Leonard Spencer-Churchill held many political and cabinet positions. He served as President of the Board of Trade, Home Secretary and First Lord of the Admiralty as part of the Asquith Liberal government. A noted statesman and orator, Churchill was also an officer in the British Army, a historian, writer and artist.
column5: Winston Churchill, estadista y orador extraordinario -  primer ministro británico que lideró a su país con firmeza inquebrantable hasta derrotar al Eje.

column2: Benito Amilcare Andrea Mussolini was an Italian politician who led the National Fascist Party and is credited with being one of the key figures in the creation of Fascism. He became the 40th Prime Minister of Italy in 1922 and began using the title Duce by 1925.
column5: Fundador del fascismo y gobernante de Italia como "Duce" desde los años veinte, persiguió sueños imperiales mediante campañas agresivas en el Mediterráneo.

column2: Franklin Delano Roosevelt was the 32nd President of the United States and a central figure in world events during the mid-20th century, leading the United States during a time of worldwide economic crisis and world war. FDR's combination of optimism and economic activism is often credited with keeping the country's economic crisis from developing into a political crisis.
column5: F. D. Roosevelt, 32.º presidente de EE. UU., afrontó la Gran Depresión e introdujo al país en el conflicto mundial convirtiéndolo en el arsenal aliado.

column2: The Showa Emperor was the 124th emperor of Japan according to the traditional order. His reign began on December 25, 1926 and encompassed a period of tremendous change in Japanese society.
column5: Emperador Showa de Japón a partir de 1926 -  símbolo de la nación nipona durante una época de auge militarista, industrialización y expansionismo en Asia.

column2: Albert Speer was a German architect a member of Hitler's inner circle. Speer construct a number of structures, including the Reich Chancellery and the Zeppelinfeld stadium in Nuremberg where Party rallies were held. He also made plans to reconstruct Berlin on a grand scale, with huge buildings, wide boulevards, and a reorganized transportation system.
column5: Arquitecto del círculo cercano de Hitler que, al asumir el ministerio de armamento, reorganizó de forma eficiente la producción de guerra alemana.

column2: Emiliano Zapata was one of the leading figures in the Mexican Revolution. He inspired, formed and led the Liberation Army of the South and his main demands and slogan was 'Reform, Freedom, Justice and Law!' which refered to the need for an agrarian reform in favor of the farmers and the need for free elections. Since military supplies were lacking then whole strategy of the Zapatistas was succesfully based on guerilla warfare.
column5: Emiliano Zapata, figura clave de la Revolución mexicana y jefe del Ejército del Sur, abanderó la reforma agraria y libró una eficaz guerra de guerrillas.

column2: Emiliano Zapata organized both a succesfull guerilla war against the federal forces and managed to introduce popular social reforms in the regions held by the Zapatistas. The power of his Liberation Army of the South was largerly based on his charisma, guerilla strategy and the support from the lower classes of the society.
column5: Líder zapatista con hondo arraigo campesino que aplicó repartos agrarios y medidas sociales en Morelos mientras contenía a las tropas federales.

column2: Guerilla warfare is a form of irregular warfare which is mainly based on such military tactics as ambushes, sabotage, raids or surprise hit and run attacks and extraordinary mobility. Fighting forces usually consist of small, mobile, lightly armed groups, that take advantage of terrain and usually have support of the local population. But it has been succesfully used on divisional and army level as well. Such warfare often is asymmetrical being engaged against better equipped enemy, though guerilla warfare proved to be effective even in the face of ever more sophisticated warfare tools and strategies of the 20th century. The term of guerilla fighters is traced back to Spanish bands who effectively opposed Napoleon.
column5: Doctrina de guerra irregular basada en emboscadas, sabotaje y movilidad extrema de unidades ligeras apoyadas por el terreno y la población local.

column2: A planned economy is an economic system in which decisions regarding production and investment are embodied in a plan formulated by a central authority, usually by a government agency.
column5: Defiende la economía planificada en la que los objetivos de fabricación, recursos e inversión se fijan directamente desde organismos centrales del Estado.

column2: Keynesian economics argues that private sector decisions sometimes lead to inefficient macroeconomic outcomes and, therefore, advocates active policy responses by the public sector, including monetary policy actions by the central bank and fiscal policy actions by the government to stabilize output over the business cycle.
column5: Promueve el gasto público anticíclico y medidas monetarias estatales para estabilizar el empleo y la producción durante las recesiones económicas.

column2: The Reformer of the Army concentrates his effort on the modernization of the armed forces.
column5: Dedica sus mayores energías a la modernización doctrinal y a la adopción de equipo militar avanzado en las fuerzas armadas.

column2: The Construction Magnate has a prominent place in the construction industry. He can use his position to increase the productivity of his industries and boost the construction of roads, airports, naval base and others infrastructures.
column5: Magnate del sector de obras que aprovecha sus constructoras para acelerar el desarrollo de puertos, aeródromos, calzadas y defensas fijas.

column2: This minister fights to have a balanced budget, with tight money, limits on welfare and foreign aid.
column5: Prioriza la austeridad fiscal, la contención del gasto público y el equilibrio estricto de las cuentas del Estado por encima de otros programas.

column2: Mixed economy is an economic system in which both the state and the private sector direct the economy, with characteristics proper of both market economies and planned economies. Most mixed economies can be described as market economies with strong regulatory oversight, in addition to having a variety of government-sponsored aspects.
column5: Partidario de combinar la iniciativa de la empresa privada con la supervisión y participación regulatoria estratégica del Estado.
Defensor de la salud y seguridad laboral

column2: Health and Safety Proponent believes that the primary purpose of a government is to improve the workers' safety and the health care system.
column5: Sostiene que el deber primordial del gobierno radica en proteger las condiciones laborales, la seguridad y el sistema sanitario de los trabajadores.

column2: The Chief of Secret Police uses his position to root out dissent and disloyal elements within the local population.
column5: Emplea los servicios de seguridad interior y la policía política para sofocar cualquier atisbo de disidencia interna y purgar traidores.

column2: This Chief of the Army belives that the use of highly trained Special Forces can make the difference in the battle.
column5: Comandante que defiende que destacamentos reducidos de élite con adiestramiento riguroso deciden el desenlace de los combates clave.

column2: This Chief of the Staff believes in the use of Special Forces and teaches that small but highly trained formations are the essence of modern warfare.
column5: Doctrina de Estado Mayor que sitúa a las unidades de comandos y fuerzas de operaciones especiales en el centro de la estrategia militar moderna.

column2: This Chief of the Staff believes in the Doctrine of Autonomy. This means that allowing the operational commanders freedom of command is essential for winning the war.
column5: Doctrina que otorga a los mandos subordinados plena iniciativa operativa sobre el terreno para reaccionar ante los imprevistos bélicos.

column2: The title of Reichskommissar was given by Adolf Hitler to a number of Nazi governors in several occupied countries during World War II. The Reichskommissars were the supreme civil authorities in their assigned territories, usually ruling with dictatorial and repressive methods.
column5: Gobernador civil plenipotenciario designado en territorios ocupados -  gobernaba con métodos dictatoriales, confiscaciones y dura represión.

column2: Captain Pieper was made responsible for the sinking of battleship SMS Yorck of which he held command. In the fog his ship collided with a German mine. To prevent being imprisoned he accepted to serve in the military mission to the Ottoman Empire, but Souchon and Usedom refused to give him any position in the staff. At that time, Ottoman's ammunition production was in very disastrous condition and Souchon convinced Enver to reorganize the whole production under the lead of Pieper. In a couple of months all factories came under German control. Because of his extraordinary contribution in this position Wilhelm II has give him a reprieve.
column5: Tras perder el SMS Yorck, el capitán Pieper reorganizó la producción de munición del Imperio otomano, pasando las fábricas a control germano y logrando el indulto imperial.

column2: Meißner was an engineer and a railway constructor. Already early in his life he decided to work in Turkey. He was chief engineer of the Hejaz Railway which was built from 1900 to 1909 and since 1910 he was responsible for the construction of the Baghdad Railway. One of the goals of the Ottoman Army was the occuaption of the Suez Canal, but the infrastructure in Palestine and Sinai were in a bad condition. From Jerusalem to the Sinai front, troops had to travel by foot on non-paved roads. Meißner was instructed by the Ottoman Army to built a military railway in this region.
column5: Ingeniero ferroviario en Oriente Próximo. El mando otomano le encomendó tender una línea férrea militar en Palestina y el Sinaí para apoyar el asalto al canal de Suez.

column2: Bronsart was part of the German military mission since her establishment in 1913 and in 1914 he became chief of staff of the Ottoman Army. He worked closely with Enver, the Ottoman war minister and generalissimo. He had bad relations with the head of military mission Liman von Sanders, which cause his replacement in 1917 by Hans von Seeckt.
column5: Llegó a Turquía en 1913 y ejerció como jefe de Estado Mayor del ejército otomano. Sus discrepancias con Liman von Sanders precipitaron su relevo por Hans von Seeckt en 1917.

column2: At the beginning of the Great War Seeckt was chief of staff of the III. Armee-Korps. Since 1915 he was chief of staff under general Mackensen and in 1917 he joined the German military mission and replaced Bronsart von Schellendorf as chief of staff of Ottoman Army. Seeckt became an important military figure in the Weimar Republic.
column5: Oficial de Estado Mayor bajo Mackensen -  en 1917 asumió la jefatura de Estado Mayor otomana en relevo de Bronsart. Más tarde sería una figura militar clave de la República de Weimar.

column2: Souchon was made commander of German naval forces in the Mediterranean (Mittelmeerdivision) in 1913. At the outbreak of the war he bombarded some ports on Algerian coast and fled from British Navy to Constantinople where he handed over his squadron to the Ottoman Navy. The Ottoman Empire expelled Admiral Limpus – who held the command of Ottoman fleet hitherto – and his British Naval Mission. Souchon was made supreme commander of the Ottoman Navy.
column5: Comandante naval que evadió a los británicos hasta Constantinopla para transferir sus buques. Tras expulsar a la misión británica, asumió el mando supremo de la armada otomana.

column2: In 1917 Wilhelm Souchon became commander of the High Seas Fleet (Hochseeflotte) when Rebeur-Paschwitz took over his command as chief of Ottoman Navy. Before he was commander of the II. Squadron (II. Geschwader).
column5: Oficial al mando de la escuadra naval en el Imperio otomano hasta que en 1917 fue transferido de regreso a Alemania para asumir el mando en la Flota de Alta Mar.

column2: Serno was one of the first pilots of military aircrafts. He received his pilot's licence in 1912 and so he ranked to the so-called Old Eagles (Alte Adler). In October 1914 he joined the German military mission as squadron leader and he convinced the Ottoman military leadership to establish an air force. Serno was made Chief of Frontline Aviation (Feldflugchef) in 1915 and was then responsible for training and organization. It was his idea to give the pilots a distinct uniform (a winged crescent and star on their hats).
column5: Pionero de la aviación que convenció a los otomanos de fundar su propia fuerza aérea en 1914. Como jefe de la aviación de campaña, estandarizó su instrucción y organización.

column2: Goltz joined the German Military mission in 1917. He was made General Inspector of the Ottoman Naval Air Force.
column5: Oficial germano incorporado a la misión militar en 1917 para desempeñarse como inspector general de las nacientes fuerzas aeronavales del Imperio otomano.

column2: The 2nd department of the Ottoman war ministry was responsible for Intelligence. In 1915 Lt. Colonel Sievert was made its chief of operations and organized paramilitary units.
column5: Asignado en 1915 a la segunda sección del Ministerio de Guerra otomano, dirigió las operaciones de espionaje y organizó unidades paramilitares de contrainsurgencia.

column2: Thauvenay was a globetrotter. He took part on the expedition to surpress the Boxer Rebellion and from 1907 to 1911 he was an advisor in the Argentinian Army. In 1913 he joined the German military mission to the Ottoman Empire and when war started back in Germany he was made company commander. He rejoined the military mission in 1915 as chief of intelligence and communication.
column5: Veterano de misiones en China y Argentina que se unió al contingente en Turquía en 1913. En 1915 asumió la jefatura de los servicios de información y transmisiones militares.

column2: Usedom retired as vice-admiral in 1910. When in August 1914 the Ottoman Empire requested a compensation for the recently dismissed British naval mission headed by admiral Limpus, the German Empire immediately sent a mission – the so called Imperial Navy's Special Command Unit in Turkey (Sonderkommando der Kaiserlichen Marine in der Türkei) - to Istanbul headed by the reactivated Guido von Usedom. This mission was responsible for the defence network of the Dardanelles.
column5: Vicealmirante reactivado en 1914 al frente del comando especial naval en Turquía para sustituir la asesoría británica y fortificar la red defensiva de los Dardanelos.

column2: Since 1912 admiral Limpus was the head of the British naval mission to the Ottoman Empire. He was an advisor for the Ottoman navy ministry and was the supreme commander of the Ottoman fleet. He was dismissed as supreme commander during the negotiations between the German admiral Souchon – who arrived in Istanbul with his fleet – and the Ottoman leadership. The Ottoman Empire canceled the British naval mission on 15th August 1914 and Limpus left Turkey one month later.
column5: El almirante Limpus asesoró a la marina otomana hasta el estallido bélico de 1914, cuando la llegada de la flota alemana provocó la expulsión de la delegación británica.

column2: Heinrich Himmler was Reichsführer of the SS, a military commander and a leading member of the Nazi Party. As Chief of the German Police and later the Minister of the Interior, Himmler oversaw all internal and external police and security forces, including the Gestapo (Secret State Police).
column5: Jefe de las SS y ministro del Interior del Tercer Reich. Ejerció un control absoluto sobre la policía estatal, los servicios de seguridad interior y los campos de concentración.

column2: Wilhelm Frick was a prominent German Nazi official serving as Minister of the Interior of the Third Reich. Frick took a leading part in Germany's re-armament in violation of the Versailles Treaty. He drafted laws introducing universal military conscription and extending the military service law to Austria after the Anschluss, as well as to the annexed regions of Czechoslovakia.
column5: Ministro del Interior nazi que orquestó la legislación para el rearme alemán, la conscripción obligatoria universal y la absorción territorial de Austria y Checoslovaquia.

column2: Wilhelm Canaris was a German admiral, head of the Abwehr, the German military intelligence service, from 1935 to 1944 and member of the German Resistance.In 1937 he was still a supporter of Hitler, considering him to be the only solution against communism and a hope for the national revival of Germany. By 1938, however, he had realised that Hitler's policies and plans would lead Germany to disaster and secretly began to work against the régime.
column5: Jefe de la Abwehr (1935-1944). Pese a servir al régimen, se desilusionó tempranamente del liderazgo nazi y operó encubierto en contacto con la resistencia militar alemana.

column2: Heydrich was a high-ranking German Nazi official. He was chief of the Reich Main Security Office (including the SD, Gestapo and Kripo and Deputy Reich-Protector of Bohemia and Moravia. Heydrich and his SD successfully convinced Joseph Stalin that the leadership of the Red Army was planning a coup in the Soviet Union. This lead to the Great Purge of the Soviet military that resulted in the execution of Mikhail Tukhachevsky and seven other top Soviet commanders.
column5: Jefe de la RSHA y viceprotector de Bohemia y Moravia. Hábil manipulador de inteligencia, represor implacable y ejecutor clave del aparato de exterminio nazi.

column2: He was a German diplomat remembered mostly for having served as Foreign minister of Germany between 1932 and 1938. Holding this post in the early years of Adolf Hitler's regime, Neurath was regarded as playing a key role in the foreign policy pursuits of the Nazi dictator in undermining the Treaty of Versailles and territorial expansion in the prelude to World War II, although he was often averse tactically if not necessarily ideologically.
column5: Diplomático tradicional y ministro de Exteriores (1932-1938) -  facilitó la revisión del Tratado de Versalles y dio una apariencia moderada al expansionismo alemán inicial.

column2: Joachim von Ribbentrop was Foreign Minister of Germany from 1938 until 1945. Ribbentrop played a key role in the conclusion of a Soviet-German non-aggression pact, the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact, in 1939, and in the diplomatic action surrounding the attack on Poland.
column5: Ministro de Asuntos Exteriores alemán entre 1938 y 1945. Negoció el pacto germano-soviético de no agresión de 1939 y articuló las maniobras previas a la invasión de Polonia.

column2: Commander-in-Chief of the Luftwaffe, President of the Reichstag, Prime Minister of Prussia and, as Hitler's designated successor, the second man in the Third Reich. Goering distinguished himself as an air ace, credited with shooting down twenty-two Allied aircraft. Awarded the Pour le Merite and the Iron Cross (First Class), he ended the war with the romantic aura of a much decorated pilot and war hero.
column5: Comandante de la Luftwaffe y segundo hombre del Tercer Reich. Antiguo as de caza de la Gran Guerra, promovió una doctrina agresiva de supremacía aérea y prestigio personal.

column2: Martin Bormann was a prominent Nazi official. He became head of the Party Chancellery and private secretary to Adolf Hitler. He gained Hitler's trust and derived immense power within the Third Reich by controlling access to the Führer and by regulating the orbits of those closest to him.
column5: Jefe de la Cancillería del Partido y secretario privado de Hitler. Amasó gran poder fáctico al controlar de manera implacable el acceso personal al Führer y la agenda del régimen.

column2: During World War II, Goebbels increased his power and influence through shifting alliances with other Nazi leaders. By late 1943, the tide of the war was turning against the Axis powers, but this only spurred Goebbels to intensify the propaganda by urging the Germans to accept the idea of total war and mobilization. Goebbels remained with Hitler in Berlin to the end.
column5: Ministro de Propaganda del Tercer Reich. Maestro de la manipulación de masas, orquestó la censura informativa estatal y promovió la movilización fanática para la guerra total.

column2: In 1938 Todt founded the Organisation Todt proper as a consortium of the administrative offices which Todt had personally set up in the course of the Autobahn project, private companies as subcontractors and the primary source of technical engineering expertise. In 1941 Todt and his organization were further charged with a large project, the construction of an Atlantic wall to be built on the coasts of occupied France, the Netherlands, and Belgium.
column5: Ingeniero y ministro de Armamento. Fundó la organización de ingeniería y obras militares encargada de levantar las autopistas, la Línea Sigfrido y el Muro Atlántico.

column2: Stanley Baldwin was a British Conservative politician, statesman and Prime Minister. Baldwin was essentially a One Nation Conservative. The onset of the Second World War would change his public image for the worse. Rightly or wrongly, Baldwin, along with Chamberlain and MacDonald, was held responsible for the United Kingdom's military unpreparedness on the eve of war in 1939.
column5: Primer ministro conservador británico señalado por la opinión pública por descuidar el gasto militar defensivo y la preparación de las fuerzas armadas antes de 1939.

column2: Admiral Sir Hugh Sinclair was a British intelligence officer. Between 1919 and 1921, he was Director of British Naval Intelligence, and helped to set up the Secret Intelligence Service (SIS, commonly MI6) before the Second World War. In 1938, with a second war looming, Sinclair set up Section D, dedicated to sabotage. In spring of 1938, using his own money, he bought Bletchley Park to be a wartime intelligence station.
column5: Director del servicio de inteligencia naval y posterior jefe del MI6. Promovió la sección de sabotaje y adquirió con fondos propios las instalaciones clave de Bletchley Park.

column2: Neville Chamberlain was a British Conservative politician who served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from May 1937 to May 1940. Chamberlain is best known for his appeasement foreign policy, and in particular for his signing of the Munich Agreement in 1938, conceding the Sudetenland region of Czechoslovakia to Germany.
column5: Primer ministro británico (1937-1940). Pasó a la historia por su política exterior de apaciguamiento y la firma de los Acuerdos de Múnich frente al expansionismo germano.

column2: The Viscount Halifax from 1934 until 1944, was one of the most senior British Conservative politicians of the 1930s, during which he held several senior ministerial posts, most notably as Foreign Secretary from 1938 to 1940. As such he is often regarded as one of the architects of the policy of appeasement prior to World War II.
column5: Secretario de Asuntos Exteriores británico entre 1938 y 1940. Considerado uno de los principales arquitectos diplomáticos de la política de apaciguamiento frente al Eje.

column2: Gian Galeazzo Ciano was an Italian Minister of Foreign Affairs and Benito Mussolini's son-in-law. After 1939, Ciano became increasingly disenchanted with Nazi Germany and the course of World War II, although when the Italian regime embarked in the ill-advised parallel war alongside Germany, he went along fairly convinced, even through the terribly-devised Italian invasion of Greece and its subsequent setbacks. Ciano was effectively executed for dissenting against the Duce's will.
column5: Ministro de Asuntos Exteriores italiano y yerno de Mussolini. Pese a sus dudas sobre el poderío nazi, respaldó la entrada en la guerra hasta su distanciamiento del Duce.

column2: Benito Mussolini was an Italian politician who led the National Fascist Party and is credited with being one of the key figures in the creation of Fascism. Mussolini pushed for government control of business: by 1935, Mussolini claimed that three quarters of Italian businesses were under state control. He also attempted to turn Italy into a self-sufficient autarky, instituting high barriers on trade with most countries except Germany.
column5: Mussolini impulsó el control estatal de las industrias y barreras al comercio exterior para imponer una economía autosuficiente y volcada en la producción militar.

column2: Alberto Pariani was an Italian general. He fought during World War I, and ended the war as a commander of the 6th Alpini Regiment. From 1934 to 1936 he was Deputy Chief of the General Staff, and from 1936 to 1939 he was Chief of the General Staff and Under-Secretary of War.
column5: General alpino y jefe de Estado Mayor italiano entre 1936 y 1939. Diseñó las reformas doctrinales y la reestructuración binaria de las divisiones del ejército de tierra.

column2: Domenico Cavagnari was an Italian admiral. He became the chief of staff of the Italian Navy in 1934 and later became the Undersecretary of State governing naval affairs. He was credited with shaping the Italian Navy into a strong force in the Mediterranean Sea, but in fact it was his fault for not introducing naval aviation to Italy. He also opposed the use of radars and carriers.
column5: Jefe de Estado Mayor naval italiano en los años treinta. Fomentó los acorazados, pero retrasó la introducción del radar, los portaaviones y la aviación naval embarcada.

column2: In foreign policy, Mussolini soon shifted from the anti-imperialism of his lead-up to power to an extreme form of aggressive nationalism. He dreamt of making Italy a nation that was 'great, respected, and feared' throughout Europe, and indeed the world. His first steps into foreign policy seemed to portray him as a 'statesman'. Following the Stresa Front against Germany in 1935, Mussolini's policy took a dramatic turning point and revealed itself once again to be that of an aggressive nature.
column5: Reorientó la política exterior italiana hacia un expansionismo bélico en África y el Mediterráneo con el fin de emular la hegemonía del antiguo Imperio romano.

column2: Maxim Litvinov was a Russian revolutionary and prominent Soviet diplomat. In 1930, Joseph Stalin appointed Litvinov as People's Commissar for Foreign Affairs. A firm believer in collective security, Litvinov worked very hard to form a closer relationship with France and Britain. In 1933 he successfully persuaded the United States to officially recognize the Soviet government and then he facilitated the acceptance of the USSR into the League of Nations in 1934.
column5: Comisario de Asuntos Exteriores soviético defensor de la seguridad colectiva. Logró el reconocimiento diplomático de EE. UU. y el ingreso de la URSS en la Sociedad de Naciones.

column2: Lazar Kaganovich was a Soviet politician and administrator and one of the main associates of Joseph Stalin. In 1930, Kaganovich became a member of the Soviet Politburo and the First Secretary of the Moscow Obkom of the Communist Party. He also supervised the implementation of many of Stalin's economic policies, including the collectivization of agriculture and rapid industrialization. From 1937 to 1939, he served as Narkom (minister) for Heavy Industry. During 1939–1940, he served as Narkom for the Oil Industry.
column5: Estrecho colaborador de Stalin y comisario de Industria Pesada. Aplicó con brutal eficiencia las directrices de colectivización forzosa y la industrialización acelerada.

column2: Genrikh Yagoda was a Soviet state security official who served as director of the NKVD, the Soviet Union's Stalin-era security and intelligence agency, from 1934 to 1936. Appointed by Joseph Stalin, Yagoda supervised the arrest, show trial, and execution of the Old Bolsheviks Lev Kamenev and Grigory Zinoviev in 1936, events that manifested the beginnings of the Great Purge. However, he was then arrested and found guilty of treason and conspiracy at the Trial of the Twenty One in March 1938.
column5: Director del NKVD entre 1934 y 1936. Supervisó los primeros arrestos y juicios farsa del régimen estalinista, hasta que cayó en desgracia y fue ejecutado en 1938.

column2: Mikhail Tukhachevsky was a Marshal of the Soviet Union, commander in chief of the Red Army (1925–1928), and one of the most prominent victims of Joseph Stalin's Great Purge. Tukhachevsky was given a leading role in reforming the army. He held advanced ideas on military strategy, particularly on the use of tanks, motorized infantry and aircraft in combined operations.
column5: Mariscal soviético y reformador castrense. Desarrolló la doctrina de operaciones en profundidad, coordinando blindados, infantería motorizada y aviación de asalto.

column2: Chairman of the Council of People's Commissars
column5: Presidente del Consejo de Comisarios del Pueblo

column2: Vyacheslav Mikhailovich Molotov was a Soviet politician and diplomat, an Old Bolshevik and a leading figure in the Soviet government from the 1920s to the 1950s. From December 1930 to May 1941 Molotov headed the Soviet government as Chairman of the Council of People's Commissars. Stalin also made Molotov responsible for the process of so-called 'collectivization of agriculture' in which peasants were integrated into collective farms belonging to the state (which however caused a widespread famine in Ukraine in 1932-33). Molotov also oversaw the implementation of the First Five-Year Plan for rapid industrialisation.
column5: Político y diplomático soviético de máxima confianza de Stalin. Dirigió el Sovnarkom, supervisó planes de industrialización y firmó el pacto germano-soviético de 1939.

column2: Cordell Hull was an American politician from the U.S.. He is best known as the longest-serving Secretary of State. Hull tried to consolidate the defense system of his country, increasing diplomatic relations with allied countries. Hull was the underlying force and architect in the creation of the United Nations, as recognized by the 1945 Nobel Prize for Peace.
column5: Secretario de Estado estadounidense de mayor permanencia. Promovió la ayuda a las naciones aliadas y fue el principal arquitecto diplomático para la fundación de la ONU.

column2: Henry Morgenthau, Jr. was the U.S. Secretary of the Treasury during the administration of Franklin D. Roosevelt. He played a major role in designing and financing the New Deal. Morgenthau believed in balanced budgets, stable currency, reduction of the national debt, and the need for more private investment. Morgenthau was an orthodox economist who opposed Keynesian economics.
column5: Secretario del Tesoro bajo Roosevelt. Financió el New Deal y el esfuerzo bélico aliando la intervención estatal con presupuestos equilibrados y estabilidad monetaria.

column2: John Edgar Hoover was the first director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) of the United States. Appointed director of the Bureau of Investigation —predecessor to the FBI— in 1924, he was instrumental in founding the FBI in 1935, where he remained director until his death in 1972. Hoover is credited with building the FBI into a large and efficient crime-fighting agency, and with instituting a number of modern innovations to police technology.
column5: Primer director del FBI entre 1935 y 1972. Transformó la agencia en un organismo de contrainteligencia y persecución penal moderno mediante técnicas centralizadas.

column2: William Friedman was a US Army cryptographer who ran the research division of the Army's Signals Intelligence Service (SIS) in the 1930s, and parts of its follow-on services into the 1950s. In 1940, a team lead by him and Frank Rowlett broke Japan's PURPLE cipher, thus disclosing Japanese diplomatic secrets.
column5: Criptógrafo militar estadounidense al frente del SIS. Lideró los equipos de descifrado que rompieron el código diplomático japonés PURPLE antes de la Segunda Guerra Mundial.

column2: Henry Lewis Stimson was a Republican Party politician who served twice as Secretary of War (in 1911–1913 and in 1940–1945). After World War II broke out in Europe, President Franklin D. Roosevelt returned Stimson, then aged 73, to his post at the head of the War Department. During the war, Stimson directed the expansion of the military, managing the conscription and training of 13 million soldiers and airmen and the purchase and transportation to battlefields of 30 percent of the nation's industrial output.
column5: Secretario de Guerra de EE. UU. (1940-1945). Dirigió el alistamiento de millones de reclutas y la reconversión de la industria para abastecer a las tropas en frentes globales.

column2: Edward Stettinius Jr. was United States Secretary of State under Presidents Franklin D. Roosevelt and Harry S. Truman, serving from 1944 to 1945. Stettinius, as chairman of the US delegation to the United Nations Conference on International Organization, was instrumental in the formation of the United Nations and was present at its official founding on June 26, 1945.
column5: Secretario de Estado bajo Roosevelt y Truman. Presidió la delegación de EE. UU. en San Francisco, siendo decisivo en la redacción de la Carta fundacional de la ONU.

column2: Harold LeClair Ickes was a United States administrator and politician. In 1933 Roosevelt appointed Ickes as his Secretary of the Interior. This involved running the Public Works Administration (PWA) and over the next six years spent more than $5,000,000,000 on various large-scale projects. Ickes, a strong supporter of civil rights, worked closely with Walter Francis White of the NAACP to establish quotas for African American workers in PWA projects. He also obtained concession from the Saudi Arabian government for the extraction of oil.
column5: Administrador clave del New Deal como jefe de Obras Públicas y secretario del Interior. Coordinó la explotación petrolera y promovió la equidad en el empleo civil.

column2: Vincent Jules Auriol was a French politician who rose to prominence as the Socialists' spokesman on financial affairs. He served as chairman of the Chamber's finance committee in 1924-26 and then as Minister of Finance in the Popular Front government of Leon Blum in 1936-37. His 30 percent devaluation of the franc against the dollar in September 1936 spurred capital flight and economic uncertainty that contributed to Blum's downfall in the spring of 1937.
column5: Ministro de Finanzas del Frente Popular francés (1936-1937). Su devaluación del franco buscaba dinamizar la producción, pero desató fuga de capitales e incertidumbre.

column2: Marx Dormoy was a French socialist politician, noted for his opposition to the far right. From 1936 to 1938 he was Minister of the Interior, and fought the rise of violent far right groups such as the Cagoule. He was also an opponent of illegal immigration of Eastern European political refugees to France.
column5: Ministro del Interior socialista de Francia (1936-1938). Combatió a grupos armados clandestinos de extrema derecha como La Cagoule y reforzó el orden público republicano.

column2: Maurice Gustave Gamelin was a French general. Gamelin is best remembered for his unsuccessful command of the French military in 1940 during the Battle of France and his steadfast defense of republican values. In 1933 Gamelin rose to command the French Army and oversaw the completion of the Maginot Line defense.
column5: Comandante supremo francés en 1939-1940. Planteó una estrategia militar conservadora basada en la invulnerabilidad de la Línea Maginot y el despliegue estático de reservas.

column2: Maurice Gustave Gamelin was a French general. Gamelin is best remembered for his unsuccessful command of the French military in 1940 during the Battle of France and his steadfast defense of republican values. Gamelin's vision for France's defense was based upon a static defense along the Franco-German border. In September 1939, he ordered his troops back behind the Maginot Line and chose defend the Ardennes with only ten reserve divisions as he considered them impenetrable.
column5: Generalísimo francés de doctrina rígida. Desestimó la velocidad de las divisiones acorazadas alemanas y consideró infranqueable el sector boscoso de las Ardenas.

column2: Yvon Delbos was a French Radical-Socialist Party politician and minister.In January 1937, in reply to Hitler's Reichstag speech of the previous day, Deblos emphasised the need for Franco-German understanding and for both countries to find new markets so that industrial expansion might replace rearmament. M.Delbos expounded French Foreign Policy in a debate in the Chamber on November 18 - 19, emphasizing Anglo-french friendship and the necessity for its maintenance. He then visited central and eastern European capitals to foster friendly relations with those countries.
column5: Ministro de Asuntos Exteriores galo en el Frente Popular. Buscó distender fricciones con Alemania, asegurar la alianza con Gran Bretaña y estrechar lazos con Europa Oriental.

column2: Georges Bonnet was a French politician and a leading figure in the Radical-Socialist Party. He was appointed Finance Minister on 28 June 1937. Bonnet's first major act as Finance Minister was to oversee the devaluation of the franc (the second devaluation in less than nine months). Bonnet then imposed sharp cuts in military spending as he felt that the costs of the arms race with Germany were such that it was better for France to reach an understanding that might end the arms race rather than investing in the military.
column5: Ministro francés que impuso recortes presupuestarios en defensa para priorizar la estabilidad financiera, promoviendo pactos de apaciguamiento para eludir el rearme.

column2: Hideki Tojo was a general of the Imperial Japanese Army (where he was known as Razor), the leader of the Taisei Yokusankai, and the 40th Prime Minister of Japan during most of World War II, from 17 October 1941 to 22 July 1944. As Prime Minister, he was directly responsible for the attack on Pearl Harbor, which led to the war between Japan and the United States. He continued militaristic and nationalist indoctrination in the national education system, and reaffirmed totalitarian policies in government.
column5: General y primer ministro de Japón durante la guerra en el Pacífico. Firme partidario del militarismo imperial y la represión interna, ordenó el ataque a Pearl Harbor.

column2: Yuan Shikai was an influential general in the late Qing Empire in charge of modernizing the army. He oversaw the abdication of the Qing Emperor after sensing the changing times by quickly shifting his allegiance to ''democracy.'' Neither an incompetent nor genius administrator, Yuan Shikai relied on his military clout to exploit the weakness of the new Republic for his own gain.
column5: Militar pragmático que maniobró entre la caída de la dinastía Qing y los inicios de la República, apoyándose en su ejército personal para centralizar el poder en beneficio propio.

column2: Cai E is a historic revolutionary leader who took part in various anti-Qing and pro-Republic movements. Educated in Japan, he governed various regions in southwestern China and led the Yunnan governor-generals to war against Yuan Shikai in the National Protection War. While successful at defending the fledgeling republic, Cai E's health problems prevented him from unifying the various factions in China. He died at the age of 33.
